characteristic_sites: mediastinum (very common — bulky mediastinal mass characteristic)
heme_involvement_pattern.staging_system: Lugano modification of Ann Arbor (I-IV, A/B symptoms). PET-adapted response assessment (Deauville).

biomarkers.name: CD30
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic hallmark. Brentuximab vedotin (anti-CD30 ADC) — approved for advanced-stage first-line (ECHELON-1: A+AVD improved modified PFS vs ABVD) and relapsed/refractory disease; A+AVD is an accepted front-line option for advanced disease

biomarkers.name: CD20
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishes cHL from NLPHL (which is typically CD20+)

biomarkers.name: PD-L1 amplification (9p24.1)
biomarkers.prevalence: Very common in cHL, especially 9p24.1 copy gain/amplification; not literally 95-100% by amplification testing
biomarkers.clinical_use: 9p24.1 alteration with PD-L1/PD-L2 overexpression is a hallmark of cHL and contributes to sensitivity to anti-PD-1 therapy (nivolumab, pembrolizumab). PD-1–based regimens have shown strong efficacy in advanced disease, including nivolumab + AVD in SWOG S1826

biomarkers.name: EBV (EBER ISH)
biomarkers.prevalence: ~10-25% in nodular sclerosis cHL (lower than mixed cellularity)
biomarkers.clinical_use: EBV positivity is less common in nodular sclerosis than in mixed cellularity and is more often associated with older age and certain cHL subtypes

biomarkers.name: Interim PET / Deauville score
biomarkers.clinical_use: PET-adapted therapy (e.g., RATHL, EORTC H10): Deauville 1-3 at interim is generally considered PET-negative and may permit treatment de-escalation in selected protocols; Deauville 4-5 is PET-positive and may prompt escalation depending on regimen/study

biomarkers.name: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Emerging role for response assessment and minimal residual disease monitoring

biomarkers.name: IPS (International Prognostic Score)
biomarkers.clinical_use: For advanced-stage HL: albumin, Hb, sex, age, stage IV, WBC, lymphocyte count. Prognostic tool rather than a sole determinant of treatment intensity

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Sparse Reed-Sternberg cells and lacunar Hodgkin cells in a nodular pattern separated by broad collagen bands; extensive inflammatory background
histomorphological_subtype.grading: No universally accepted histologic grading system; clinical staging is by Ann Arbor/Lugano, and IPS is used for advanced-stage prognostication

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Classical 'immune-inflamed but suppressed' paradigm — RS cells constitute <1% of tumour; the vast majority is dysregulated inflammatory infiltrate (T cells, eosinophils, plasma cells, macrophages); frequent 9p24.1 alteration with PD-L1/PD-L2 overexpression contributes to marked anti-PD-1 sensitivity
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Broad collagen bands partition tumour into nodules; lacunar cells with retracted cytoplasm in formalin-fixed tissue

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Crippled germinal centre B cells (Reed-Sternberg cells) that have lost B-cell receptor expression but escape apoptosis through EBV or recurrent pro-survival pathway alterations, especially NF-κB and JAK-STAT pathway activation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Reed-Sternberg cells retain B-cell derivation but lose most B-cell markers (CD20 often negative or dim); express CD30, CD15, PAX5 (weak); lacunar variants have retracted cytoplasm in formalin fixation
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Represents unusual B-cell state where germinal centre selection failure would normally trigger apoptosis, but pro-survival alterations (NF-κB pathway activation, JAK-STAT activation, 9p24.1/PD-L1-PD-L2 copy gain or amplification) rescue crippled B cells; loss of B-cell programme (CD20, immunoglobulin) reflects lineage-relevant reprogramming
